## Context

Large ticket descriptions materially degrade both plan review and completion verification. The existing P4 description signal is advisory at 24,000 characters, above the historical maximum, so it cannot protect either gate.

Historical replay is complete and recorded in the ticket comments. The corpus covered 2,202 work tickets, 4,037 plan-review events, and 1,121 completion-verifier events. Current descriptions were p99 7,500 characters and maximum 15,853. At 8,000 characters, only 18/2,202 tickets (0.82%) were affected, while plan-review latency was materially worse and completion PASS rates were lower. The operator selected 8,000 as a generous blocking maximum.

This decision supersedes the old requirement that P4 never block. Other P4 signals remain advisory. This ticket does not add fuzzy severity labels, vacuity heuristics, or a second oversize criterion.

## Plan

- Add a typed [verify] maximum-description setting with a default of 8,000 characters. Exactly 8,000 characters is allowed; 8,001 blocks. Document the setting and require a positive integer.
- Keep description sizing in p4_oversize. A description above the configured maximum makes the P4 result blocking; AC-count and file-impact signals remain advisory and continue accumulating into the same P4 finding.
- In the light bug-review arm of workflow_ops.plan_review_precheck, partition DET blocks: retain only a blocking P4 description finding in det_blocking and downgrade every other DET block to advisory as before. Let that retained finding flow into the shared deterministic short circuit so an oversized light-tier bug returns BLOCK with coverage.llm_ran=false. Non-bug and blast-radius-escalated bug paths continue using the shared short circuit directly.
- In completion verification, check the authoritative ticket description after loading the same [verify] setting and before child checks or context assembly. Return the existing validated deterministic FAIL shape with an actionable split/shorten finding and make zero runner calls.
- Do not truncate, summarize, or elide ticket content. A ticket must be reduced below the maximum before either gate runs; force remains the operator escape hatch already provided by lifecycle commands.
- Add focused boundary, configuration, bug-tier, no-LLM-call, and advisory-regression tests. Keep the historical completion-recovery tests intact because they exercise the lower-level full-context recovery mechanism, not admission of a newly oversized ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The default maximum description length is 8,000 characters and is configurable through typed [verify] configuration.
- [x] A description of exactly 8,000 characters is admitted and a description of 8,001 characters is blocked.
- [x] Plan review returns a deterministic BLOCK with coverage.llm_ran=false before any LLM call when a work ticket exceeds the maximum.
- [x] The blocking plan-review behavior applies to bug, story, task, and epic tickets; light bug review retains the P4 description block while downgrading other DET blocks.
- [x] Completion verification returns a validated deterministic FAIL with zero runner calls when the authoritative ticket description exceeds the maximum.
- [x] AC-count and file-impact P4 signals remain advisory when the description is within the maximum.
- [x] P4 still emits at most one oversize finding, including when several size signals are present.
- [x] Neither gate truncates, summarizes, or elides ticket content to get under the maximum.
- [x] Documentation explains the default, the strict greater-than boundary, the historical calibration, and the existing force override.
- [x] [operator-attested] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, and the non-integration/non-external suite pass.
